name: BTC at N-day maximum (trend leg)
author: Quantpedia
summary: Hold BTC only on days when the close is at its rolling N-day maximum; shorter lookbacks work best and the rule cuts drawdowns versus buy-and-hold.
notes: Exit not stated explicitly; read as daily re-evaluation (hold while at max). Revisited in 2024 article with same rule (quantpedia.com/revisiting-trend-following-and-mean-reversion-strategies-in-bitcoin/).

name: BTC MAX + MIN combined
author: Quantpedia
summary: Hold BTC when it closes at its N-day max (trend) or N-day min (mean reversion); claimed 98% annual return, 48% vol, -38% max DD 2015-2022.
notes: Exit inferred as daily re-evaluation; formulas in source are images.

name: Catching Crypto Trends (Donchian close breakout, midpoint trailing stop)
author: Carlo Zarattini, Alberto Pagani, Andrea Barbon
summary: Long when close exceeds max close over lookback; trailing stop at midpoint of max/min closes; ensemble of lookbacks 5-360 days with 25% vol target; Sharpe >1.5 net claimed.
notes: Single-lookback version; ensemble of 9 lookbacks, the ratchet (stop = max(prior stop, midpoint)), 25% vol targeting with 200% leverage cap and altcoin rotation not expressible. Paper summary also at concretumgroup.com.

name: Price above prior-day SMA (crypto)
author: Trinh Hue Le, Ummul Ruthbah
summary: Hold BTC/ETH only when price is above its prior-day SMA (20/65/150/200), otherwise cash; tested net of 0.1-0.5% costs.
notes: Paper: Trend-following Strategies for Crypto Investors. 150-day window also tested.

name: DEMA short/long crossover on BTC
author: L. Mo, L. Wang, Z. Zhang, K. Huang
summary: Long when short double-exponential MA exceeds long DEMA (short 1-20, long 21-50 days); DEMA version most stable Sharpe in BTC bear markets.
long_entry: (2 * ema(close, s) - ema(ema(close, s), s)) > (2 * ema(close, l) - ema(ema(close, l), l))
long_exit: (2 * ema(close, s) - ema(ema(close, s), s)) < (2 * ema(close, l) - ema(ema(close, l), l))
notes: Best pairs not reported in summary; grid picked from stated ranges. Same paper also tests SMA and EMA crosses.

name: Donchian 15 breakout with low-ADX filter
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Buy BTC when close breaks the 15-day high while ADX(14) < 25 (breakout from quiet market); exit on close below 15-day low; ~90% CAGR vs 66% B&H claimed.
notes: Channel defined on highs/lows assumed (source says 15-day high/low).

name: Bitcoin MACD histogram sign
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Long BTC while MACD histogram is positive, exit when negative; 77% CAGR 2015-2024 claimed.
notes: Page behind bot check; rules from indexed takeaways (positive histogram = entry, negative = exit), standard 12/26/9 assumed.

name: Multi-timeframe MACD (daily filter, hourly trigger)
author: Quantpedia
summary: Daily MACD>signal as trend filter, hourly MACD cross as entry, exit on first negative hourly bar; Sharpe 1.07 vs 0.33 for pure hourly MACD.
notes: Needs hourly bars; daily-only part reduces to the daily MACD cross (see trend-qs-btc-macd-histogram).

name: 9 EMA close cross
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Buy BTC when close is above the 9-day EMA, sell when below; 284 trades, 2.65% avg gain, 83% max DD since 2014.
notes: Site also tested 20-day EMA (optimum 5 days, 145% CAGR) in its BTC trend article; grid covers both.

name: 9 EMA with 200 SMA regime filter
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Same 9-EMA close rule but entries only when close is above the 200-day SMA, cutting drawdown.
notes: Exit assumed same as base rule.

name: BTC 100/250 SMA crossover
author: QuantifiedStrategies
summary: Long when 100-day SMA is above 250-day SMA; 115% CAGR vs 94% B&H 2015-2021 with only three trades, 65% max DD.
notes: Rules from indexed snippet; page behind bot check.

name: Pi Cycle Top exit
author: Philip Swift
summary: 111-day SMA crossing above 2x the 350-day SMA has marked BTC cycle tops within 3 days; used as a hold-until-top exit.
notes: Indicator only flags tops; entry rule (re-enter once 111 SMA is back below 2x350 SMA) is our reading, which makes the book long almost always.

name: Mayer Multiple 2.4 rule
author: Trace Mayer
summary: Price / 200-day SMA; accumulate below a threshold and sell above 2.4 (historical overbought; 0.8 oversold).
notes: Original claim: buying below 2.4 historically best; 0.8/2.4 bands from Glassnode description.

name: Bull market support band (20W SMA / 21W EMA)
author: Benjamin Cowen / Into The Cryptoverse
summary: BTC is in a healthy bull trend while above the 20-week SMA / 21-week EMA band; losing it preceded multi-month weakness.
notes: Weekly MAs approximated with daily windows (x7) on daily closes; source evaluates weekly closes.

name: 20-week / 50-week SMA bullish cross
author: U.Today
summary: 20-week SMA crossing above 50-week SMA has preceded protracted BTC uptrends in past cycles.
notes: Weekly MAs approximated as 7x daily windows; exit on reverse cross assumed.

name: Golden cross / death cross (SMA)
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: Bullish when the 50-day SMA crosses above the longer SMA (golden cross), bearish on the reverse death cross.
notes: ChartSchool example uses 50/100; the classic golden cross is 50/200, both in grid.

name: Golden/death cross long-short
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: Same 50/200 SMA cross but taking the death cross as a short signal, i.e. always in the market in the cross direction.
notes: Source describes the death cross as bearish; shorting it is the literal long/short reading.

name: 5-8-13 EMA stack
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: Short-term trend from three EMAs (5, 8, 13); bullish when stacked fast over slow.
notes: Source gives no explicit entry/exit; stacked-order entry and fast-cross exit are the standard reading.

name: Moving average ribbon alignment (20-65)
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: Ten SMAs 20..65 step 5; trend is strong and up when shorter averages sit above longer ones in order.
notes: Ribbon reduced to 4 of the 10 averages; ribbon width/expansion reading not encoded.

name: Moving Momentum (20/150 SMA + stochastic pullback + MACD-hist)
author: StockCharts ChartSchool (Arthur Hill)
summary: Trade with the 20/150 SMA bias: buy after a stochastic pullback below 20 when MACD histogram turns positive; mirror for shorts.
notes: Source has no explicit exit (uses support/resistance stops); exit on opposite MACD-hist sign assumed. 'Recent' stochastic dip taken as within 10 days.

name: Slope performance trend (absolute + relative slope)
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: Buy when both the 12-month regression slope of price and of the price relative to the benchmark are positive; sell when both negative.
notes: Linear-regression slope sign approximated by comparing the mean of the last 180 days to the prior 180; S&P 500 used as benchmark (original: sector vs SPY on monthly charts).

name: Trend quantification (PPO 50 vs long EMAs)
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: Four PPO(50,L) with L=125/150/175/200; each positive adds 25% equity exposure, all negative = out.
notes: Fractional 25% scaling not expressible; each single PPO leg given as a binary rule via the grid.

name: Six-month cycle MACD (Sy Harding)
author: Sy Harding
summary: Be long only in the Oct 16 - Apr 20 favourable season, timing entry and exit with MACD signal crosses.
notes: Equity seasonal from Riding the Bear; MACD 12/26/9 assumed (source does not give periods); zero-line alternative omitted.

name: MACD zero-line cross with swing breakout
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: Go long when MACD and signal are above zero and price breaks a prior swing high; trail stop under swing lows.
notes: Swing highs/lows approximated by n-day channel; MACD 12/26/9 assumed.

name: Ichimoku cloud trend (price above green cloud)
author: Goichi Hosoda
summary: Uptrend when price is above the cloud and Span A > Span B; downtrend below a red cloud.
notes: Assumes ichi_span_a/b return the cloud value plotted at today (i.e. computed 26 bars ago); 9/26/52 defaults.

name: Ichimoku Tenkan/Kijun cross in trend
author: Goichi Hosoda
summary: Classic signal: in an uptrend (price above cloud) buy when Conversion Line crosses above Base Line; sell on the reverse cross.
notes: Long-only reading; short side mirrors below the cloud.

name: Ichimoku close crosses Base Line in uptrend (scan)
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: StockCharts scan: close above Span B, Span A above Span B, and close crosses back above the Base Line after a pullback.
notes: Exit on close below Base Line assumed (scan has no exit).

name: Chandelier exit stop-and-reverse
author: Charles Le Beau
summary: Long exit at 22-day high minus 3 ATR(22); a break above the short chandelier (22-day low + 3 ATR) signals strength.
notes: Chandelier is an exit; entry on break above the short-side chandelier follows the page's 'signals strength' reading. Year approximate.

name: Hull moving average turning points
author: Alan Hull
summary: Use HMA turning points (not crossovers) for entries and exits; HMA = WMA(sqrt n) of 2*WMA(n/2) - WMA(n).
long_entry: wma(2 * wma(close, 10) - wma(close, 20), 4) > shift(wma(2 * wma(close, 10) - wma(close, 20), 4), 1)
long_exit: wma(2 * wma(close, 10) - wma(close, 20), 4) < shift(wma(2 * wma(close, 10) - wma(close, 20), 4), 1)
notes: HMA(20) (StockCharts default) written out with fixed numbers since n/2 and sqrt(n) cannot be param-derived.

name: Hull MA(55) turning points
author: Alan Hull / StockCharts
summary: Slower HMA used for trend direction: long while a longer HMA is rising.
long_entry: wma(2 * wma(close, 27) - wma(close, 55), 7) > shift(wma(2 * wma(close, 27) - wma(close, 55), 7), 1)
long_exit: wma(2 * wma(close, 27) - wma(close, 55), 7) < shift(wma(2 * wma(close, 27) - wma(close, 55), 7), 1)
notes: Source says longer HMAs show the trend; 55 is our chosen length (popular TradingView default), noted as such.

name: KAMA price crossover with KAMA trend filter
author: Perry Kaufman
summary: Price crossing KAMA(10,2,30) gives entries, with a slower KAMA(10,5,30) defining the trend.
notes: KAMA is a recursive adaptive filter (efficiency-ratio-driven smoothing constant); vocabulary has no recursive or variable-alpha MA.

name: Keltner channel breakout (Raschke ATR version)
author: Chester Keltner / Linda Raschke
summary: Uptrend starts when price breaks above the upper Keltner channel (20 EMA + 2 ATR); downtrend on break below the lower.
notes: Source ATR length is 10 vs EMA 20; kc_up(n,k) uses one n. Exit at middle line assumed (source gives none).

name: Keltner ten-day moving average trading rule (1960)
author: Chester W. Keltner
summary: Center = 10-day SMA of typical price, bands = +/- 10-day SMA of high-low range; buy close above upper band, sell close below lower.
long_entry: close > sma((high + low + close) / 3, 10) + sma(high - low, 10)
long_exit: close < sma((high + low + close) / 3, 10) - sma(high - low, 10)
short_entry: close < sma((high + low + close) / 3, 10) - sma(high - low, 10)
short_exit: close > sma((high + low + close) / 3, 10) + sma(high - low, 10)
notes: Stop-and-reverse reading of the band signals.

name: Parabolic SAR stop-and-reverse
author: J. Welles Wilder
summary: Always in the market on the side of the parabolic SAR (step 0.02, max 0.20); reverses when price crosses SAR.
notes: Assumes psar_dir returns +1 when SAR below price. From New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems.

name: Parabolic SAR with ADX trend filter
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: Act on SAR flips only when ADX shows a trending market (SAR works in the ~30% of time markets trend).
notes: Page suggests ADX filter qualitatively; thresholds from ADX article (20/25).

name: Donchian 20-period channel breakout (long/short)
author: Richard Donchian
summary: Long on a break above the 20-period high, short on a break below the 20-period low; one backtest reports 35% win rate and 2:1 payoff.
notes: Stop-and-reverse; StockCharts price-channels page notes channels exclude the current bar, matching lag 1.

name: Wilder DMI crossover with ADX confirmation
author: J. Welles Wilder
summary: Buy when +DI crosses above -DI with ADX above 20-25; sell when -DI crosses above +DI with ADX confirming.
notes: Wilder's signal-day-low stop (extreme point rule) not expressible; DI reversal used as exit.

name: DMI cross with 50-day SMA filter
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: SharpCharts example: take +DI/-DI buy signals only when price is above its 50-day SMA and ADX > 20.
notes: Exit assumed: DI reversal or loss of 50-SMA.

name: Aroon trend bias (Up>50, Down<50)
author: Tushar Chande
summary: Uptrend when Aroon-Up(25) > 50 and Aroon-Down < 50 (recent 25-day high fresher than the low).
notes: Aroon-Up > 50 rewritten as 'the 26-bar high occurred within the last 13 bars' (no days-since function in vocabulary).

name: Coppock curve zero cross (monthly, scaled to days)
author: Edwin Coppock
summary: Buy when the 10-month WMA of ROC(14m)+ROC(11m) turns from negative to positive; analysts sell on the reverse.
notes: Monthly periods converted at 30 days/month on daily bars; Coppock only used the buy signal (Barron's 1965).

name: Pring KST signal-line cross (daily)
author: Martin Pring
summary: Weighted sum of four smoothed ROCs; bullish when KST crosses above its 9-period SMA signal.
long_entry: (sma(roc(close, 10), 10) + 2 * sma(roc(close, 15), 10) + 3 * sma(roc(close, 20), 10) + 4 * sma(roc(close, 30), 15)) > sma(sma(roc(close, 10), 10) + 2 * sma(roc(close, 15), 10) + 3 * sma(roc(close, 20), 10) + 4 * sma(roc(close, 30), 15), 9)
long_exit: (sma(roc(close, 10), 10) + 2 * sma(roc(close, 15), 10) + 3 * sma(roc(close, 20), 10) + 4 * sma(roc(close, 30), 15)) < sma(sma(roc(close, 10), 10) + 2 * sma(roc(close, 15), 10) + 3 * sma(roc(close, 20), 10) + 4 * sma(roc(close, 30), 15), 9)
notes: Daily default KST(10,15,20,30,10,10,10,15,9); Stocks & Commodities 1992.

name: TRIX signal-line cross
author: Jack Hutson
summary: TRIX = 1-day % change of triple-smoothed 15 EMA; bullish when it crosses above its 9 EMA signal.
notes: TRIX(15,9) defaults.

name: TRIX centerline cross
author: Jack Hutson
summary: Bullish momentum while TRIX(15) is above zero, i.e. the triple-smoothed EMA is rising.
long_entry: ema(ema(ema(close, n), n), n) > shift(ema(ema(ema(close, n), n), n), 1)
long_exit: ema(ema(ema(close, n), n), n) < shift(ema(ema(ema(close, n), n), n), 1)
notes: TRIX > 0 is equivalent to the triple EMA rising day over day.

name: Vortex indicator with 1.10/0.90 thresholds
author: Etienne Botes, Douglas Siepman
summary: Bullish when -VI(14) weakens below 0.90 and +VI(14) strengthens above 1.10; bearish when -VI crosses above +VI.
long_entry: (sma(abs(high - shift(low, 1)), 14) / sma(max(high, shift(close, 1)) - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 14) > 1.1) & (sma(abs(low - shift(high, 1)), 14) / sma(max(high, shift(close, 1)) - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 14) < 0.9)
notes: VI computed exactly: ratio of 14-day sums equals ratio of 14-day means; TR built from high/low/prior close.

name: Vortex +VI/-VI crossover
author: Etienne Botes, Douglas Siepman
summary: Trend is up while +VI(14) is above -VI(14), down when below (Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities, Jan 2010).
long_entry: sma(abs(high - shift(low, 1)), n) > sma(abs(low - shift(high, 1)), n)
long_exit: sma(abs(high - shift(low, 1)), n) < sma(abs(low - shift(high, 1)), n)
short_entry: sma(abs(high - shift(low, 1)), n) < sma(abs(low - shift(high, 1)), n)
short_exit: sma(abs(high - shift(low, 1)), n) > sma(abs(low - shift(high, 1)), n)
notes: TR denominator cancels in the +VI vs -VI comparison.

name: TTM Squeeze breakout
author: John Carter
summary: Buy the first bar the squeeze fires (Bollinger 20/2 leaves Keltner 20/1.5) with momentum above zero; exit when momentum fades two bars.
long_exit: ((close - ((highest(high, 20) + lowest(low, 20)) / 2 + sma(close, 20)) / 2) < shift(close - ((highest(high, 20) + lowest(low, 20)) / 2 + sma(close, 20)) / 2, 1)) & (shift(close - ((highest(high, 20) + lowest(low, 20)) / 2 + sma(close, 20)) / 2, 1) < shift(close - ((highest(high, 20) + lowest(low, 20)) / 2 + sma(close, 20)) / 2, 2))
notes: Momentum histogram's linear-regression smoothing omitted (raw deviation used); squeeze tested on upper bands only; StockCharts Keltner uses SMA+ATR whereas kc_up may be EMA-based. From Mastering the Trade.

name: MACD-V rallying zone
author: Alex Spiroglou
summary: Volatility-normalised MACD ((EMA12-EMA26)/ATR26*100); 'rallying' when between 50 and 150 and above its 9 EMA signal (Dow Award paper).
notes: Source defines lifecycle zones, not explicit trades; entering in the rallying zone and exiting below the signal line is our reading of the defaults.

name: Williams Alligator awakening
author: Bill Williams
summary: Smoothed MAs of median price (13/8/5, shifted 8/5/3); enter when Lips > Teeth > Jaw (awake/hungry), exit when lines converge/cross back.
long_entry: (shift(ema((high + low) / 2, 9), 3) > shift(ema((high + low) / 2, 15), 5)) & (shift(ema((high + low) / 2, 15), 5) > shift(ema((high + low) / 2, 25), 8))
short_entry: (shift(ema((high + low) / 2, 9), 3) < shift(ema((high + low) / 2, 15), 5)) & (shift(ema((high + low) / 2, 15), 5) < shift(ema((high + low) / 2, 25), 8))
notes: SMMA(n) approximated as EMA(2n-1); fractal entry trigger omitted. From Trading Chaos.

name: Elder Impulse System with long-term trend
author: Alexander Elder
summary: Green bar = 13 EMA rising and MACD-hist rising; buy when long-term trend (MACD(1,65,1) > 0) is up and impulse turns green; sell when red.
notes: MACD(1,65,1) > 0 equals close above 65 EMA. From Come Into My Trading Room.

name: Robot Wealth crypto breakout feature (days since 20-day high)
author: Robot Wealth
summary: Crypto alpha scored as 9.5 minus days since the 20-day closing high; positive score = recent high, predicts returns across crypto assets.
notes: Continuous score turned into a sign rule (score > 0 means the 20-day high was within the last 10 days); original is a cross-sectional weight.

name: Faber 10-month SMA timing (month-end)
author: Mebane Faber
summary: Hold the asset when its month-end close is above the 10-month SMA, else cash; equity-like returns with bond-like volatility and drawdowns across asset classes.
notes: A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation. 10 months ~ 300 daily bars on a 7-day market; 12-month variant (365) also cited by StockCharts. Signal checked only on the last day of the month.

name: Brock-Lakonishok-LeBaron variable moving average (VMA)
author: William Brock, Josef Lakonishok, Blake LeBaron
summary: Buy when the short MA (1-5 days) is above the long MA (50-200) by more than a band, sell when below; strong predictability on the DJIA 1897-1986.
notes: Simple Technical Trading Rules and the Stochastic Properties of Stock Returns (J. Finance). Original rule set (1,50),(1,150),(5,150),(1,200),(2,200) with 0/1% band; grid is the cross product. Corbet et al. (2019) found the VMA rule best on high-frequency BTC.

name: Trading range breakout on BTC
author: Dirk Gerritsen, Elie Bouri, Ehsan Ramezanifar, David Roubaud
summary: Of seven trend rules on daily BTC 2010-2019, trading range breakout had the most forecasting power and beat buy-and-hold on bootstrapped Sharpe, especially in strong trends.
notes: The profitability of technical trading rules in the Bitcoin market (FRL). Parameters follow the Brock et al. (1992) TRB family the paper builds on; BLB's fixed 10-day holding replaced by opposite-break exit.

name: High-frequency BTC MA-oscillator and TRB rules
author: Shaen Corbet, Veysel Eraslan, Brian Lucey, Ahmet Sensoy
summary: On high-frequency BTC returns, moving-average rules are significant and the variable-length MA rule performs best; buy signals earn more than sell signals.
notes: Intraday data; the daily analogue of the winning rule is trend-blb-variable-ma.

name: Hudson-Urquhart 15,000 technical rules on crypto
author: Robert Hudson, Andrew Urquhart
summary: Nearly 15,000 rules in five classes (MA, filter, S&R, channel breakout, OBV) are significant and profitable on BTC and other coins in-sample, but show no out-of-sample predictability for Bitcoin.
notes: A rule universe with data-snooping tests, not a single strategy; important negative OOS evidence for BTC.

name: Time-series momentum (12-month sign)
author: Tobias Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse Pedersen
summary: Long an asset whose past 12-month excess return is positive, short when negative; significant across 58 futures markets.
notes: Excess over T-bills ignored; vol scaling to 40% not expressible. Paper studies 1-48 month lookbacks; 12 months is the headline.

name: AQR century trend (1/3/12-month combo, majority vote)
author: Brian Hurst, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse Pedersen
summary: Equal-weight 1-, 3- and 12-month time-series momentum; positive in every decade since 1880.
notes: Equal-weight sum of three signals approximated by a 2-of-3 majority; long-only; vol scaling omitted.

name: BTC short-horizon time-series momentum (1-4 weeks)
author: Yukun Liu, Aleh Tsyvinski
summary: Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency: strong time-series momentum in BTC; past 1-4 week returns predict next-week returns.
notes: Paper reports predictive regressions; the sign rule is the natural strategy reading. Weekly rebalancing not enforced.

name: Clenow core trend model (50/100 EMA filter + 50-day breakout + 3 ATR trail)
author: Andreas Clenow
summary: Long on a 50-day closing high when 50 EMA > 100 EMA (short mirror); exit on a 3-ATR move against the position from its peak.
notes: Following the Trend. Peak-since-entry approximated by the 50-day high; ATR(100) per author's comment; 20bp-risk ATR sizing omitted.

name: Seykota simple exponential crossover
author: Ed Seykota
summary: Long-only: buy when fast EMA crosses above slow EMA, sell on the reverse; featured 15/150, best runs around 85/325 (13.6x stake).
notes: Trading System Primer; tested on futures with 50% skid fills.

name: Seykota support/resistance system (trend 120 / trade 30)
author: Ed Seykota
summary: Long-term trend from 120-day channel; in an uptrend buy breaks of 30-day resistance with stop at 30-day support; mirror for shorts.
notes: Seykota's trend state (up after break of 120-day resistance until break of support) needs memory; approximated by price vs the 120-day channel midpoint.

name: Elder ADX turn-up timing
author: Alexander Elder
summary: Best buy signal when ADX turns up from below both DI lines with +DI above -DI; sell when ADX turns down.
notes: From Trading for a Living as summarised on Wikipedia; 14-period default assumed.

name: Ichimoku full confirmation (cloud + TK + Chikou)
author: Goichi Hosoda
summary: Buy when price is above the cloud, Tenkan above Kijun, and the Chikou span (today's close) is above price 26 bars ago; Kijun as trailing stop.
notes: Combination of the rules the article lists; Kijun trailing stop as exit.

name: Ichimoku modern daily settings 8/21/42
author: Goichi Hosoda (modern variant)
summary: Ichimoku with shortened 8/21/42 periods for modern daily charts; long above the cloud with Tenkan above Kijun.
long_entry: ((highest(high, 8) + lowest(low, 8)) / 2 > (highest(high, 21) + lowest(low, 21)) / 2) & (close > shift(((highest(high, 8) + lowest(low, 8)) / 2 + (highest(high, 21) + lowest(low, 21)) / 2) / 2, 21)) & (close > shift((highest(high, 42) + lowest(low, 42)) / 2, 21))
notes: Lines built from highest/lowest because ichi_* functions have fixed 9/26/52; cloud displaced by 21 bars.

name: MACD zero-line cross
author: Gerald Appel
summary: Bullish when the MACD line (12 EMA - 26 EMA) crosses above zero, bearish below; slower than signal-line crosses.
notes: Equivalent to a 12/26 EMA crossover.

name: Bitcoin Investor Tool: 2-year MA multiplier
author: Philip Swift
summary: Accumulate when price is below the 2-year MA, take profit when price reaches 5x the 2-year MA.
notes: x5 is the published top band; lower multiples selectable on the chart (3 added).

name: Golden Ratio Multiplier (350DMA x Fibonacci)
author: Philip Swift
summary: Multiples (1.6, 2, 3, 5...) of the 350-day MA mark cycle-high resistance; each cycle tops at a lower multiple.
notes: Page gives no explicit buy rule; entry below the 350DMA (x1 line) is our reading.

name: 200-week MA heatmap
author: Plan B (@100trillionUSD), adapted by Look Into Bitcoin
summary: BTC has bottomed near the 200-week MA every cycle; buy near it, sell when the 200WMA's monthly growth overheats (red).
notes: Colour thresholds not published; grids are our guesses around the visible red zone. 200 weeks = 1400 daily bars.

name: Pi Cycle top and bottom oscillator
author: Look Into Bitcoin (after Philip Swift)
summary: Buy when the 111DMA sits at a 75% discount to 2x350DMA (bear lows), sell when 111DMA reaches 2x350DMA (cycle top).
notes: Oscillator formula not printed; '75% discount' read as 111DMA < 0.25 x (2x350DMA).

name: Hash Ribbons buy signal
author: Charles Edwards (Capriole)
summary: Buy when the 30-day hash-rate SMA crosses back above the 60-day (miner capitulation ends) and price momentum turns up.
notes: Needs on-chain hash rate, not in vocabulary.

name: Halving clock cycle timing
author: Quantpedia
summary: MA-based cycle signals (Mayer 2.4, Pi Cycle) went silent at the Oct-2025 top, while tops land 525-546 days after a halving and bottoms ~364-406 days after tops.
notes: Out at the post-halving top window, back in after the typical bear duration (top + ~364-406 days). Only three cycles; author flags retrospective turn identification.

name: Silicon vs Satoshi: QQQ/BTC Donchian rotation
author: Quantpedia
summary: Hold whichever of QQQ/BTC closes above its prior w-day max (priority order), else cash; Sharpe 1.4-1.7, max DD ~18-24% 2019-2025.
notes: Needs a tradable QQQ leg; the BTC-only leg reduces to trend-quantpedia-btc-at-max.

name: Dual momentum between gold and Bitcoin
author: Quantpedia
summary: Weekly: hold IBIT or GLD, whichever has the higher positive X-week return (4-12 weeks), else cash; 8-week version 80% CAGR, Sharpe 1.64.
notes: Gold series not in vocabulary; BTC absolute-momentum leg alone is close to trend-liu-tsyvinski-weekly-momentum.

name: Supertrend stop-and-reverse
author: Olivier Seban
summary: ATR band around hl2 that ratchets with the trend; a close beyond the line flips the trend (typical defaults ATR 10, multiplier 3).
notes: Assumes supertrend_dir returns +1 in uptrend. Year approximate.

name: Trend Safety Switch (Supertrend + risk-off votes)
author: oridahari
summary: Long-only Supertrend(10,3) with ADX>=15, forced flat when 2 of 3 risk-off warnings fire (VIX rank >= 80, close < 200 SMA, >15% below 1-year high).
notes: VIX 252-bar percentile rank >= 80 approximated by z-score > 0.84; 30% residual hold on healthy down-flips not expressible (all-out used). Built for equities, 252-bar windows kept.

name: ADX for BTC
author: PineIndicators
summary: Long BTC when ADX(14) crosses above 14 (trend starting), exit when ADX crosses below 45 (trend exhausted).
notes: Optional long-term SMA filter omitted (effective period unclear on page).

name: Bitcoin Momentum Strategy (weekly 20 EMA + ATR swing trail)
author: ZenAndTheArtOfTrading
summary: Long BTC while above the weekly 20 EMA and not in 'caution'; trail stop 1 ATR(5) below the 7-bar swing high, tightened to 0.2 ATR in caution.
long_exit: (close < highest(high, 7) - atr(5)) | (((highest(high, 7) - low > 1.5 * atr(5)) | (close < ema(close, 20))) & (close < highest(high, 7) - 0.2 * atr(5)))
notes: Weekly 20 EMA approximated by daily EMA(140); trailing stop ratchet replaced by the current swing-high-minus-ATR level.

name: BTC Trend-Momentum (200 EMA + CMF + StochRSI)
author: SystemsOverFeelings
summary: Long above the 200 EMA when Chaikin Money Flow is positive and StochRSI %K crosses up out of oversold; short mirror; always reverses on opposite signal.
long_entry: (close > ema(close, 200)) & (sma(((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low) * volume, 20) > 0) & cross_above(sma((rsi(close, 14) - lowest(rsi(close, 14), 14)) / (highest(rsi(close, 14), 14) - lowest(rsi(close, 14), 14)), 3), 0.2)
long_exit: (close < ema(close, 200)) & (sma(((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low) * volume, 20) < 0) & cross_below(sma((rsi(close, 14) - lowest(rsi(close, 14), 14)) / (highest(rsi(close, 14), 14) - lowest(rsi(close, 14), 14)), 3), 0.8)
short_entry: (close < ema(close, 200)) & (sma(((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low) * volume, 20) < 0) & cross_below(sma((rsi(close, 14) - lowest(rsi(close, 14), 14)) / (highest(rsi(close, 14), 14) - lowest(rsi(close, 14), 14)), 3), 0.8)
short_exit: (close > ema(close, 200)) & (sma(((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low) * volume, 20) > 0) & cross_above(sma((rsi(close, 14) - lowest(rsi(close, 14), 14)) / (highest(rsi(close, 14), 14) - lowest(rsi(close, 14), 14)), 3), 0.2)
notes: CMF sign computed exactly (sign of the numerator); CMF 20, StochRSI 14/14/3 and 0.2/0.8 levels are standard defaults since the page omits them; timeframe unspecified.

name: Turtle System 1 (20-day breakout, 10-day exit)
author: Richard Dennis / William Eckhardt (Turtles)
summary: Enter long on a new 20-day high (short on 20-day low), exit on a 10-day opposite extreme, 2N stop, ATR(N) sizing.
notes: Page gives the 20-day entry; 10-day exit, 2N stop and the skip-after-winning-breakout filter are from Faith's Way of the Turtle / Covel's Complete TurtleTrader. Skip filter, 2N stop, pyramiding and N-sizing not expressible.

name: Turtle System 2 (55-day breakout, 20-day exit)
author: Richard Dennis / William Eckhardt (Turtles)
summary: Slower Turtle system: enter on 55-day breakouts, exit on 20-day opposite breakouts, every signal taken.
notes: Exit lengths per the published Turtle rules (Faith 2007); 2N stop and unit pyramiding omitted.

name: NR7 narrow-range breakout
author: Toby Crabel
summary: After the narrowest range of 7 days, buy a move above that day's high (Aroon trend filter), trail a 2-ATR stop.
notes: Crabel took profit at first profitable close (needs entry price, not expressible); ATR trailing-stop alternative used; Aroon-Up > Aroon-Down approximated.

name: Stochastic Pop and Drop
author: Jake Bernstein / David Steckler
summary: With 70-day stochastic > 50 and ADX(14) < 20, buy when 14-day stochastic surges above 80 on above-average volume; exit when it drops below 50; mirror for drops.
notes: Stocks & Commodities Aug 2000 (Steckler); Parabolic SAR trailing stop alternative not combined.

name: Bollinger Band squeeze breakout
author: John Bollinger
summary: A new advance starts with a squeeze (BandWidth near its 6-12 month low) followed by a close above the upper band.
long_entry: (lowest((bb_up(close, 20, 2) - bb_lo(close, 20, 2)) / sma(close, 20), 10) <= lowest((bb_up(close, 20, 2) - bb_lo(close, 20, 2)) / sma(close, 20), m) * 1.1) & (close > bb_up(close, 20, 2))
notes: 'Near the low' = BandWidth within 10% of its m-day low sometime in the last 10 days; exit at middle band assumed (source has none). Bollinger on Bollinger Bands.

name: Dual MACD (weekly entry, daily/weekly exit)
author: Trading_Solutions_
summary: Long crypto when the weekly MACD crosses above its signal; exit when either the weekly or daily MACD crosses below its signal; reported good on BTC, ETH and majors.
notes: Weekly MACD(12,26,9) approximated with daily periods x7; entry taken as weekly MACD above signal (state) since the daily exit can fire inside the weekly window. Year approximate.

name: Average highest-high / lowest-low swinger
author: exlux
summary: Long when close is above both a fast and a slow (highest high + lowest low)/2 midline, short when below both; reverse on opposite signal.
long_entry: (close > (highest(high, f) + lowest(low, f)) / 2) & (close > (highest(high, s) + lowest(low, s)) / 2)
long_exit: (close < (highest(high, f) + lowest(low, f)) / 2) & (close < (highest(high, s) + lowest(low, s)) / 2)
short_entry: (close < (highest(high, f) + lowest(low, f)) / 2) & (close < (highest(high, s) + lowest(low, s)) / 2)
short_exit: (close > (highest(high, f) + lowest(low, f)) / 2) & (close > (highest(high, s) + lowest(low, s)) / 2)
notes: Lengths not stated on page; grid is our guess.

name: Glow Ribbon Flip (EMA21 +/- 2 ATR10 stop-and-reverse)
author: blitz_locked
summary: Ratcheting ATR band around a 21 EMA; a close beyond the opposite band flips long/short; re-enter on pullback closes back across the EMA.
notes: Band ratchet, pullback re-entries, 2R target and 1% risk sizing not expressible.

name: TEMA 20/50 crossover
author: Patrick Mulloy
summary: Bullish when the 20-day TEMA crosses above the 50-day TEMA; signals come earlier than EMA or DEMA crosses.
long_entry: (3 * ema(close, 20) - 3 * ema(ema(close, 20), 20) + ema(ema(ema(close, 20), 20), 20)) > (3 * ema(close, 50) - 3 * ema(ema(close, 50), 50) + ema(ema(ema(close, 50), 50), 50))
long_exit: (3 * ema(close, 20) - 3 * ema(ema(close, 20), 20) + ema(ema(ema(close, 20), 20), 20)) < (3 * ema(close, 50) - 3 * ema(ema(close, 50), 50) + ema(ema(ema(close, 50), 50), 50))
notes: TEMA = 3*EMA1 - 3*EMA2 + EMA3 (Stocks & Commodities 1994).

name: Moving average envelope breakout
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: A strong move above the upper 20-day SMA +2.5% envelope can start an extended uptrend; a plunge below the lower one a downtrend.
notes: Exit at the lower envelope assumed; wider envelopes added for BTC volatility.

name: Chande Trend Meter > 80
author: Tushar Chande
summary: Composite 0-100 trend score (BB position on 4 horizons, 100-day move vs stdev, RSI14, 2-day breakout); momentum traders buy scores >= 80.
notes: Component weights and scaling to 0-100 are proprietary/undocumented on the page.

name: Strategy 432 BTC Donchian breakout continuation (4H)
author: Fran_Pineda
summary: BTC/USDT 4H: long on close above prior Donchian high with ATR-sized breakout, ADX confirmation and price above EMA200; time exit or opposite break.
notes: 4H bars and undisclosed parameter values (channel length, ATR distance, ADX level, bars-held).

name: Lambert CCI +100 trend breakout
author: Donald Lambert
summary: Lambert's original use: buy when CCI surges above +100 (new uptrend), close when it falls back below +100; shorts mirror at -100.
notes: Commodities magazine 1980; Lambert original exit (back below +100) as cited in the CCI correction article; CCI indicator page adds the +/-100 trend-start reading.

name: CCI correction (trend bias + pullback)
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: With long-term CCI bullish, buy when 20-day CCI dips below -100 and then surges back above zero; bias flips when long-term CCI goes below -100.
notes: Bias memory approximated as 'CCI(100) above +100 within 60 days and not yet below -100'; source leaves exits to the trader so bias reversal used.

name: 52-week-high proximity (time-series adaptation)
author: Hong, Jordan, Liu (after George & Hwang 2004)
summary: Assets trading close to their 52-week high keep outperforming; long when price/52-week high ratio is high.
notes: Original is a cross-sectional industry long-short on US stocks; single-asset threshold rule with 10-point hysteresis is our adaptation.

name: Price channel pullback in a 200-SMA uptrend
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: Scan: in an asset above its 200-day SMA, buy the cross back above the lower 20-day price channel that ends a pullback.
notes: Scan has no exit; take profit at the upper channel or exit on loss of the 200 SMA assumed.

name: Keltner breakout followed by CCI pullback
author: StockCharts ChartSchool
summary: Bullish scan: a breakout above the upper Keltner channel 20 days ago, now a short-term oversold pullback with CCI(10) below -100.
notes: Scan only; exit at the opposite/upper channel assumed.

name: Ichimoku cloud color change (Kumo twist)
author: Goichi Hosoda
summary: Bullish change within the trend when the cloud turns from red to green (Span A crosses above Span B), favoured when price is above the cloud.
notes: Price above Base Line used as the momentum confirmation; span alignment assumes the cloud value displayed at today.

name: Price-to-MA ratio predictor (long/short)
author: Andrew Detzel, Hong Liu, Jack Strauss, Guofu Zhou, Yingzi Zhu
summary: Ratio of BTC price to its moving average predicts daily BTC returns in and out of sample; MA-ratio strategies earn alpha and higher Sharpe than buy-and-hold.
notes: Learning and predictability via technical analysis (Financial Management). Paper combines several MA ratios in a predictive regression; the long/short sign of one ratio is the simplest reading (long-only version = trend-le-ruthbah-price-above-sma).
